newsitem.title: USA: N.Korea aid to be based on humanitarian need - U.S..
newsitem.headline: N.Korea aid to be based on humanitarian need - U.S..

text.p: The United States will study an upcoming report on North Korea's food needs, and will make a decision on whether to give more aid to that country "based soley on humanitarian concerns," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Monday.
Burns said at the department's daily briefing that the UN World Food Program will soon issue a report on flood-stricken North Korea. "We will very seriously study its analysis." he said.
"We will make our decision based soley on humanitarian concerns," Burns said. There has been some criticism that Washington is delaying further aid to communist North Korea for political reasons.
North Korean officials have been talking with representatives from Cargill Inc for some weeks to work out the financing and other details of a 500,000-tonne grain shipment approved early last month.
A Cargill spokesperson told Reuters Monday that officials are still negotiating, and said, "We're looking at a couple of different things." The official declined to go into detail.
On the Cargill situation, Burns said: "We would like that deal to go forward. But we have never used food aid as a lever because we have to pay attention to humanitarian concerns."
